messages:
eve_support: FYI customer 'Clippr' reporting spikes of 504/502 for hosted inference over the last 30m. p50 fine, tails jumping to 10-15s then timeouts. They say it started after a high-concurrency marketing test. Escalating.

liam_sre: can you paste a sample request id or trace id? Also which model and region?

eve_support: trace ids: trace=trc_8a7e2f and trc_8a7e9b. Model: open-compat-13b-q4, region: us-west-2 hosted. Customer claims some requests complete instantly but others queue until timeout.

maria_prodeng: that sounds like request queue saturation + tail-latency. Any queue depth metrics? batcher backlog?

sanjay_infra: checking dashboards now.

ingress-bot: [ALERT] host-gateway P95 latency above 5s in us-west-2 (window=10m). active_queue_depth=1980, queue_capacity=2000, continuous_batch_backlog=320ms avg, max 4.8s.

sanjay_infra: confirmed — queue at ~99% capacity, many inflight long-running tokens. We're seeing continuous batching backlog spikes when many long-context requests enter.

liam_sre: probable root: large-context requests (>=6k tokens) are stalling KV cache and preventing batchers from draining. Need quick repro: can @devex_alex run a script that simulates the customer's load?

devex_alex: running a repro harness now. load pattern: 500 concurrent clients, 7% long-context (8k tokens), burst over 2 mins. I'll post logs.

devex_alex: (log snippet)
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z request_id=trc_8a7e2f path=/v1/hosted/generate duration=12.3s status=504 queue_wait=10.8s model=open-compat-13b-q4 tokens=8200
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z request_id=trc_8a7e9b path=/v1/hosted/generate duration=0.32s status=200 queue_wait=0.02s model=open-compat-13b-q4 tokens=34
```

maria_prodeng: interesting — mixed short and very long requests. continuous batching groups by latency buckets but when a long one gets in it holds slot. We throttle by queue depth but we still let a few huge contexts through causing head-of-line blocking.

liam_sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable per-tenant max-context enforcement (drop > 6k) 2) enable early-shed by longest-payload first (reject large requests during overload) 3) temporarily increase queue_capacity + add burst nodes. Which is fastest?

sanjay_infra: we can flip early-shed rule via infra flag in ~3-4 minutes. Increasing queue_capacity requires scheduler changes and warmup (20-30m). Per-tenant config can be deployed faster but may need customer coordination.

eve_support: customer wants minimal disruptions but will accept soft rejects if we provide guidance. Can we set a temporary 6k token hard reject with clear error message?

liam_sre: yes — patch to gateway to reject with 429 + body: {"error":"context_length_exceeded","max_tokens":6000} — deploying to us-west-2 now as emergency rollback-able change.

ingress-bot: deploy started: gateway/edge-flag=early_shed_large_contexts -> true (region=us-west-2) by sanjay_infra.

devex_alex: repro harness retest after flag: queue depth dropped to ~450, p95 latency back to ~420ms. No 504s observed in 10m window.

maria_prodeng: good. We still need a proper root cause: why did long requests start coincident with burst? Two hypotheses: 1) Customer traffic pattern changed (marketing test yes) 2) scheduler order changed causing larger requests to be batched earlier/less efficiently.

liam_sre: collect diagnostic artifacts: a) batcher debug dump for the period b) KV cache hit/miss rates c) node-level GC/pinning events d) router selection logs. @sanjay_infra can you fetch the batcher dumps and upload?

sanjay_infra: uploading tarball to /tmp/incident-triage/2062001234-batcher-dumps.tar.gz (link: https://internal.redwood/snap/2062001234) -- includes batcher profiles and kernel warning logs.

sanjay_infra: quick excerpt from batcher profile: 
```
batcher_cycle: 2.3ms avg, max 4.9s at 2026-03-15T14:01:58Z
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.48 -> spike correlated with long-context influx
active_pinned_buffers: 12 -> 96 (nodes experiencing pressure)
```

devex_alex: so KV cache miss spike plausible cause — long contexts evict KV entries and cause subsequent short requests to pay warm-up cost, increasing service time and widening tail. Continuous batching wants to pack requests but gets delayed waiting for long request completion.

maria_prodeng: for postmortem action items: - Improve admission control to consider token-length distribution, not just count. - Add per-tenant request-size-rate limiting and a burst token bucket. - Add emergency config to route long requests to dedicated slower pool (offpeak or dedicated instances). - Improve observability: show token-length histogram alongside queue depth in console.

eve_support: customer update: they accepted the temporary context limit, removed marketing burst, and say errors largely cleared. They asked for recommendations to avoid future incidents. I provided link to best practices and suggested dedicated capacity for sustained bursts.

liam_sre: final note: create a follow-up runbook step for "ingress overload with mixed long/short requests" and schedule a postmortem doc. tagging for triage: sev=high, impact=customer-visible, mitigated=true.

maria_prodeng: assigned owners: action items to product+infra with deadlines: admission control PR by 2026-03-20 (maria_prodeng), observability dashboard changes by 2026-03-25 (devex_alex), dedicated-route feature spec by 2026-04-01 (liam_sre).

eve_support: thanks team :thumbsup: I'll close the escalation once the customer confirms no further 5xxs.

liam_sre: marking incident note: mitigated->monitoring. Will follow up with PM/ENG for long-term fixes.

ingress-bot: Incident closed for us-west-2 alert window.
